newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq paper gives damning farewell to U.N. envoy.
newsitem.headline: Iraq paper gives damning farewell to U.N. envoy.

text.p: The newspaper of Iraq's ruling Baath party published a damning farewell on Wednesday to Rolf Ekeus, former United Nations arms inspector for Iraq.
"Is not it enough the lies you have made (about Iraq's weapons) and your vicious deeds," said al-Thawra in a poem entitled "Farewell to Ekeus".

Ekeus, who has led the U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM) in charge of dismantling Iraqi weapons of mass destruction since its founding in 1991, was replaced on Thursday by Australia's U.N. ambassador, Richard Butler.
"One like you should not be an arbitrator. You are (just like) an intrigued Zionist dagger (against Iraq)," the paper said.
"You have sold your conscience with money...and represented schemes of (Iraq's) attackers...you are pleased about the people's suffering from starvation," it said.
Iraq has frequently accused Ekeus of pursuing Washington's tough line against Baghdad. It also blamed him for prolonging sanctions, imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
